history.period: Antiquity unverified; locally believed at least 700 years old
history.summary: An old Shiva temple in the Katargam area of Surat on Kantareshwar Mahadev Road (CSV spells it 'Kanteshwar'; local sources consistently spell it Kantareshwar). No exact founding date is known; local accounts hold it to be at least 700 years old - treat as legend, not verified history. Legend says sage Kapil Muni established the shivlinga here (the Tapi Purana is cited for his ashram at the site) and that a cow led herdsmen to the linga hidden in a thorny (kantar) jungle, giving the deity its name. The adjacent Surya Kund pond is believed to have been created by Lord Rama's arrow at Kapil Muni's request during his exile, and drinking its water is believed to grant ancestors moksha. It is one of five regional 'K'-named Shiva temples (Kantareshwar at Surat, Kedarnath at Bardoli, Kadambeshwar at Balpur, Kankeshwar at Kanav, Kapileshwar at Navsari), believed locally to represent five brother forms of Shiva that unite here in Shravan. The Nagara-style temple has a large sanctum housing the Patalinga in a gold-lined pit, a marble Nandi, a Surya Narayana murti atop the main shikhara, and 12 small jyotirlinga shrines near the Surya Kund; a trishul installed around 1947 by saint Nrusinghagiri is said to extend 51 feet underground. Mahashivratri is the main festival (one local video reports 11,000+ diyas lit for the deepotsav), and the temple reportedly stays open round the clock during Shravan.

name: Kanteshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Surat is a major city in Gujarat on the banks of the Tapi River, historically one of India's most important ports under Mughal and then British rule. Today it is a thriving metropolis known worldwide as a diamond-processing and textile-manufacturing hub. The city grew from a 12th-century settlement into a Mughal port and later a British stronghold, retaining colonial-era landmarks, old-city bazaars, and a fast-developing riverfront. It is well connected by air, rail, and road to Mumbai, Vadodara, and the rest of Gujarat.

travel.road: Kantareshwar Mahadev Road, Katargam (near Narayan Nagar Society), ~9 km from central Surat; reachable by city bus and auto-rickshaw
